::: {.callout-tip}
## Why This Matters
Hua Hong's second 12-inch fab in Wuxi, financed with the largest single Big Fund-backed deal since the October 2022 US export control tightening — $4.02B new equity (Hua Hong Group, the Big Fund, and a Wuxi entity) plus $2.68B in debt. Reached production in December 2024 at a planned 83,000 wafers/month, with full-capacity ramp targeted for the end of Q3 2026 and process-equipment move-in completed by end of June 2026.
:::

*Chinese name not yet verified.*

## What does this facility make?

12-inch (300mm) wafers at mature specialty nodes (65nm, 55nm, 40nm) — power management, automotive, and analog chips, not leading-edge logic.

## Why does it matter?

Illustrates China's mature-node strategy: rather than chase export-controlled advanced lithography, state capital doubles down on nodes where China already has working equipment access. Hua Hong announced a THIRD Wuxi phase in September 2026 — a separate $2.127 billion investment, with construction having started in March 2026 — signaling this is an open-ended expansion programme rather than a one-off Phase 2 project; that Phase 3 commitment is not yet broken out as its own tracker entry.

## Project Timeline

- **Jan 2023** — Hua Hong Semiconductor, the Big Fund, and a Wuxi entity sign agreement for a $6.7 billion second 12-inch Wuxi fab (Fab9)
- **Jun 2023** — Construction of Fab9 begins
- **Sep 2023** — Fab9's main building topped out roughly 100 days ahead of schedule
- **Dec 2024** — Hua Hong Manufacturing (Wuxi) Fab9 put into production at a planned 83,000 wafers/month
- **Mar 2026** — Construction begins on a separate Wuxi Phase 3 project ($2.127 billion)
- **Jun 2026** — Fab9 process-equipment move-in completed; full-capacity ramp targeted for end of Q3 2026
- **Sep 2026** — Hua Hong Semiconductor formally announces the $2.127 billion Wuxi Phase 3 investment
